speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any sputum? Also, do you experience any chest pain or wheezing when you breathe?

speaker: Patient
text: My cough has been quite productive for the last two months, and the sputum I cough up is occasionally greenish. I also notice some wheezing when I breathe, but I don't have any chest pain, fever, or weight loss. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Since you have had a productive cough with greenish sputum and wheezing for two months, have you had any recent close contact with someone who had tuberculosis, or do you smoke?

REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture, Spirometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Spirometry: FEV1 65% of predicted, FVC 78% of predicted, FEV1/FVC Ratio 0.60 (reduced); Sputum_Culture: Not performed in current dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis with obstructive pattern (COPD). The presence of a productive cough with greenish sputum and wheezing for two months, combined with spirometry showing a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.60, strongly supports this diagnosis. Smoking history would help confirm the etiology, but the clinical and functional findings are sufficient for classification.
